# Buurtbox

> Buurtbox is a plug-and-play offline data hub for neighbourhoods. An energy-efficient local server that keeps essential information available when the internet goes down. Currently in development.

## About

Buurtbox is an open hardware and software project led by Lars Böhm. It is designed to be installed in neighbourhood and community centres in the Netherlands. The device broadcasts a local Wi-Fi network; connecting users are redirected to an offline portal with a curated dataset of public-domain and openly licensed content.

The project addresses the dependency of modern society on internet infrastructure for access to essential knowledge — Wikipedia, maps, health information, emergency protocols — and the risks this creates during power outages, cyberattacks, or natural disasters.

## Hardware

- Server: Raspberry Pi 4 or 5
- Storage: 1 TB+ SSD
- Power: High-capacity powerbank with automatic mains failover
- Power modes: standard (1–2 days on battery), 30-min button mode (1 week+), solar (indefinite)
- Future extension: LoRa transceiver for mesh networking between Buurtboxes

## Offline data available

- Full Wikipedia (Dutch and English)
- Government health information (RIVM, GGD)
- First-aid manuals and medical reference
- Offline OpenStreetMap data for local area
- Emergency response protocols and handbooks
- Public-domain e-books and audiobooks
- Public-domain cultural archive (art, music)

## Development timeline

- Month 1: Hardware procurement, data management dashboard development, partner outreach
- Month 2: Prototype build, first dataset version
- Month 3: Prototype testing and iteration, portal interface development
- Month 4: User testing preparation and pilot tests with partner
- Month 5: Test analysis and improvement planning
- Month 6: Final prototype, open-source release of dataset and code, results publication
